title: His mom came on our first date
author: Storytime
hook: My first date brought his mom. That wasn't even the weirdest part.
story: I'd been texting this guy, Evan, for three weeks. He was funny. Thoughtful. He remembered everything I told him. He even asked how my sister's surgery went. So we finally set up a dinner. I walk in, and Evan is sitting there with an older woman. He says, this is my mom, she was in the area. Okay. Weird, but sweet? But the whole dinner, Evan barely talked. He didn't know my sister's name. He didn't remember my job. His mom did. She asked about my sister's knee, my cat, my promotion. Everything I had told Evan. That's when I realized. I hadn't been texting Evan for three weeks. I'd been texting his mom. She made his profile, she picked his photos, and she did all the talking, because Evan was too shy. Evan just looked at his plate. Then his mom put her hand on mine and said, I know this is strange, but I really like you. And I have another son. Part two?
caption: I was never texting him 💀 #storytime
sound: a quirky, awkward comedy piano at very low volume
why: Dating story disasters are a rising theme, the too-good-to-be-true texting is the planted clue, and the other son line is a funny part two hook.

title: We shared credit scores before the wedding
author: Storytime
hook: My fiancee and I shared our credit scores before the wedding. Hers was perfect. Mine was a disaster. I had no idea why.
story: My fiancee Amy is a planner. Before the wedding, she said we should be completely honest about money. Debts, savings, credit scores. Everything. I said sure. I've always been careful with money. I pay everything on time. I don't even have a credit card. Her score was eight hundred and ten. Mine was four hundred and ninety. I thought it was a mistake. So Amy pulled my full credit report. There were three credit cards in my name. A car loan. A phone contract. Over thirty thousand dollars of debt, all in collections. I'd never opened any of them. Amy looked at the address on the accounts and went quiet. It was my mom's address. The first card was opened when I was seventeen. My mom had been using my name for twelve years. Every time I'd asked why the mail kept coming to her house, she said it was junk. When I called her, she didn't deny it. She cried and said she'd been planning to pay it all back before I ever found out. Amy says I need to file a police report, or I'll never fix my credit. My mom says if I report her, I'll destroy the family. What would you do?
caption: the debt wasn't mine. the name was 💳 #storytime
sound: a slow, heavy piano with a tense undertone at very low volume
why: Money transparency in relationships is a big viral driver, the mail that kept going to his mom's house is the planted clue, and the family versus fiancee dilemma forces viewers to pick a side.

title: Noise complaints while I wasn't home
author: Storytime
hook: My downstairs neighbor kept complaining about loud footsteps at night. I work night shifts. I'm never home.
story: I moved into a new flat in September. I work nights at a hospital, seven at night to seven in the morning. About a month in, my downstairs neighbor, an older lady called Mrs. Patel, left a note on my door. Please stop walking around so loudly at midnight. I laughed. I wasn't even home at midnight. I assumed she had the wrong flat. Then another note. The TV is too loud at two in the morning. Then another. Please ask your friend to stop slamming the door. I don't have a friend who visits. I live alone. So I bought a cheap camera and set it up in my living room before my shift. At twelve fifteen, my front door opened. A young guy walked in with his own key. He took off his shoes, opened my fridge, and sat on my couch to watch TV. Like he lived there. I called the police from the hospital. When they arrived, he showed them his key. He said the building manager gave it to him. Turns out the building manager is his uncle, and he'd been letting him sleep in empty flats at night. My flat wasn't empty. Part two?
caption: my neighbor was right. someone WAS there 🔑 #storytime
sound: a low, eerie suspense drone at very low volume
why: Neighbor noise complaint stories are a viral genre, the impossible complaints build mystery, and the building manager twist sets up a part two.
